title: New York Times Releases Its First Multiplayer Word Game, Crossplay
description: The New York Times' games are filled with single-player experiences, but now the news organization is launching its first two-player game as a standalone app. Starting today, NYT is inviting readers to try Crossplay, a game that should seem very familiar to anyone who has tried Words with Friends or Scrabble. Crossplay is now live, and this is how it works: Players start each game with seven letters on the same board. The object is to score points from creating words or playing off of the words that are already on the board. More points are awarded depending upon the rarity of the letter and where it's placed on a the board. Each player has a limited number of tile bags that are lost after a tile is played on the board. Once players run out of tiles, Crossplay enters one final round to give both players one last chance to succeed. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Battlefield 6 Community Update Reveals Season 2 Plans And Testing For Solo BR
description: The latest Battlefield 6 community update details some of the new content planned for Season 2, including a brand-new multiplayer map called Contaminated. The developer also teased the return of a classic Battlefield 4 map, and it gave an update on the likelihood of a solo playlist for Redsec battle royale. As previously announced, Battlefield 6's Season 2 update has been delayed, and Battlefield Studios is currently using the extra time to develop and refine the upcoming seasonal content. The new community update reveals Battlefield Labs is being used to test on one of Season 2's new maps called Contaminated. The studio says it is using the map to evaluate how vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, alongside cover and asset placement, and objective boundaries. Season 2's Containment mapThe developer says the full map reveal for Contaminated will arrive at a later date, but it did provide an image on social media for the first official look of the map, as seen in the image above. The studio also confirms that the map's size falls somewhere between Eastwood and Mirak Valley. It is also comparable to classic Battlefield maps such as St. Quentin Scar from Battlefield 1 or Arras from Battlefield 5. Contaminated will also have unique gameplay mechanics, and these will be tested in live matches within Battlefield Labs. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Xbox Developer Direct's "One More Thing" Matters More Than Ever In 2026
description: On January 22, the fourth-ever Xbox Developer Direct showcase will take place. Right now, we know that it will feature Game Freak's Beast of Reincarnation as well as Forza Horizon 6 and Fable from Playground Games. If this year's Developer Direct follows in the footsteps of every previous incarnation of the show, there's likely to be an unexpected surprise, as well. Most famously, Hi-Fi Rush was shadow-dropped during the first Developer Direct, making for one of the most exhilarating moments of the console generation for Xbox players. Moments of hope like that are few and far between for Xbox fans nowadays. As Xbox's future looks more mysterious than ever in 2026, this year's Developer Direct would really benefit by delivering a memorable "one more thing." Xbox's Developer Direct presentations trade the pace and quantity of titles from the summer Xbox Games Showcases for a more intimate, developer-focused show where studios can show off the games they are working on. For an entity as corporate as Microsoft, these shows offer up a much-needed slice of humanity and relatability. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: One Of Fallout's Most Popular Mods Won't Support Rumored Remasters
description: The benefit of Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas being as old as they are is the robust modding scene that has been built around them, giving you new ways to enjoy both classic role-playing games. It's an area where any imminent remasters will likely fall short, and that's for certain already if you're hoping for support from one of the series' most popular mods. Tale of Two Wastelands might be the most comprehensive and popular mod for both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas, seamlessly combining the two experiences into one massive, cohesive adventure across its two distinct open worlds. The mod brings the quality-of-life and gameplay updates in New Vegas and introduces them to Fallout 3, while giving you the ability to use a single character across both adventures, complete with balancing changes and enhancements to support both campaigns. Switching between the two areas is as easy as boarding a train from the arid deserts of Nevada to the derelict streets of Washington D.C., which undersells just how complicated the entire mod is to make it seem that simple. Given the amount of work that has gone into Tale of Two Wastelands over more than a decade, it should come as no surprise that its developers have no plans to replicate it should remasters for either Fallout 3 or Fallout: New Vegas manifest. Posting on the mod's official discord server (and spotted by GameSpark), one of the mod's creators laid this out plainly. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: New Fallout 76 Update Is All About Squashing Bugs, And We're Not Talking Radroaches
description: Bethesda has delivered a chunky new update for Fallout 76 that's mainly focused on fixing issues in the online RPG. One fun specific gameplay area that's addressed relates to player Ghoul characters, who now must wear a disguise to re-enter Fort Atlas and Crater Core. The patch notes highlight that the download size isn't small: It's 28.9GB on Xbox, 12.8GB on PlayStation, 14.7GB on Steam, and 26.7GB on the PC Microsoft Store. This is the first major patch for Fallout 76 since the Burning Springs update went live last month. Burning Springs brings players to a wasteland version of Ohio, with new creatures to encounter as well as The Ghoul from the Prime TV show. Yes, Walton Goggins reprises his role, but he has zero interest in playing any of the Fallout games personally. Two lingering bugs have been taken care of in Fallout 76, thanks to the patch. Bethesda was aware of them quickly after Burning Springs went live. They dealt with talking with the Rust King as a disguised Ghoul and completing Discover Locations challenges in the new map area. Both have been addressed. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Enshrouded Update Coming In Spring, Full Release Scheduled For Fall 2026
description: On January 24, 2024, Keen Games put its survival action role-playing game Enshrouded into early access. Now, to mark the impending second anniversary of its early-access release, Keen Games has announced that Enshrouded will get an update in Spring 2026 followed by the full 1.0 launch on PC and consoles in Fall 2026. In a newly- released development diary video, Enshrouded community lead François Hardy and creative director Antony Christoulakis laid out some of the changes coming to the game. The Spring 0.8 update will feature general improvements, including bug fixes and balance adjustments. The biggest addition to the game here will be "Adventure Sharing," which will let players share their world with other members of the the Enshrouded community. The Enshrouded 1.0 release will have even more refined features, including improvements for new player experiences and quest progression. Christoulakis noted that the game's combat is being retooled to give it greater tactical depth while pitting players against smarter and more varied enemies. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Unreal Engine Makes Films Look Too Much Like Games, Pirates Of The Caribbean Director Says
description: Over the last couple of years, Epic Games has made a big push into Hollywood with its Unreal Engine software. Best known as a game development engine, recent upgrades have made it a powerful tool for film and television, as seen in productions like The Mandalorian. While it has its fans, Pirates of the Caribbean director Gore Verbinski isn't one of them, likening the rise of Unreal Engine 5 in Hollywood to the "greatest slip backwards" for the moviemaking industry, resulting in films that look too much like video games. "It used to be a divide, with Unreal Engine being very good at video games, but then people started thinking maybe movies can also use Unreal for finished visual effects," Verbinski said to But Why Tho (via VGC). "So you have this sort of gaming aesthetic entering the world of cinema." As Verbinski explained, Unreal Engine 5's approach to light and its application in scenes doesn't work with films aiming for a photorealistic presentation. The filmmaker says that this tends to create an uncanny valley effect, something that human brains can pick up on very quickly when they see it in motion. Continue Reading at GameSpot
